concepts.title: Natural Hazards: Earthquakes, Tsunami, Cyclones and Floods
concepts.definition: Natural hazards include earthquakes along seismic zones, tsunamis from undersea earthquakes, tropical cyclones of the Bay of Bengal and Arabian Sea, floods and droughts from rainfall variability, and landslides in mountains, each demanding preparedness and management.
concepts.key_idea: India's seismic zoning marks the most quake-prone Himalayan belt, and the east coast faces frequent tropical cyclones in the retreating monsoon season.

concepts.title: Disaster Management and Mitigation
concepts.definition: Disaster management moves through prevention, mitigation, preparedness, response and recovery, using early warning systems, cyclone shelters, land use regulation, relief and rehabilitation to reduce losses from natural hazards.
concepts.key_idea: Community preparedness with warning dissemination and rescue training converts hazards from disasters into manageable events.

concepts.title: Vulnerability Zones and Community Preparedness
concepts.definition: India's hazard vulnerability is mapped into seismic zones with the Himalayan belt in the most severe zone, a cyclone prone east coast, flood plains of the Ganga-Brahmaputra and drought prone arid tracts, so vulnerability zoning with community preparedness reduces disaster losses.
concepts.key_idea: Knowing the vulnerable zone lets authorities plan building codes, shelters and evacuation routes before the hazard strikes.
